Container.Name: TucanoTime
Container.Overview: TucanoTime is a self-hosted timesheet server: one Rust binary serves the REST API, the browser GUI and the OpenAPI docs. Data is file-based JSON, so there is no database. The published image is distroless (no shell, no package manager) and runs as the fixed non-root user 10001:10001; the Unraid Console button will therefore not open a terminal, which is expected. Use docker logs TucanoTime from an Unraid terminal instead. First run: open the WebUI and complete the admin startup wizard (administrator, then company, then currency). All persistent state lives on the /data path.
Container.Description: TucanoTime timesheet server (API, GUI and contract in one binary). Container hardening is intentional: ExtaParams adds --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges, so the root filesystem is read-only, every Linux capability is dropped and privilege escalation is blocked. /data is the only writable bind mount and /tmp is a small tmpfs. The runtime image has no shell; the Unraid Console will not work by design. On first start open http://[IP]:[PORT:8080]/ and complete the admin startup wizard (administrator, then company, then currency); then use Settings, Email to configure SMTP. Set TUCANO_SECURE_COOKIES=0 for plain HTTP on the LAN (the template default); set it to 1 only when the WebUI is served over HTTPS. The credential vault generates /data/vault.key automatically on first boot; TUCANO_SECRET_KEY(_FILE) is only an optional external override. If secrets.bin exists but no key can open it, the app refuses to start instead of silently losing access. See deploy/unraid/README.md in the repository for the full runbook.

Config.Name: Data (all persistent state)
Config.Description: Holds every document the app writes: customers, projects, entries, invoices, users, config.json, session.key, secrets.bin, the generated vault.key, audit.log and scheduler state. It must be owned by uid/gid 10001 because the image is fixed non-root; run: chown -R 10001:10001 /mnt/user/appdata/tucanotime before the first start. Back up this whole folder: it contains both the encrypted vault and the key that decrypts it, so protect the backup accordingly (or keep the key outside /data with an external override).

Config.Name: WebUI port
Config.Description: Host port published to the container on 8080. Open http://YOUR-UNRAID-IP:8080/ after the container starts. In bridge mode this is reachable from the LAN by default; restrict it with a firewall or put it behind a TLS reverse proxy if that matters.

Config.Name: Data dir (internal)
Config.Description: Internal data directory inside the container. Leave at /data; it must match the Data path target above. This is the TUCANO_DATA_DIR environment variable read by src/main.rs.

Config.Name: Listen port (internal)
Config.Description: TCP port the server binds inside the container and the port the image HEALTHCHECK probes. Leave at 8080 and change the WebUI port mapping instead if you need a different host port.

Config.Name: Plain-HTTP cookies
Config.Description: Cookie Secure flag, independent of TUCANO_ENV. 0 drops the Secure attribute so login works over plain http://YOUR-UNRAID-IP:8080. Set to 1 only when the WebUI is served over HTTPS (for example behind a TLS reverse proxy); with 1 over plain HTTP the browser discards the session cookie and login loops.

Config.Name: Vault key file (optional override)
Config.Description: Leave empty to let the app create and manage /data/vault.key automatically on first boot (32 base64url characters, mode 0600). Set this only to supply an external key from outside the data directory, for example a Docker secret mounted into the container: the path must name a file holding exactly 32 ASCII bytes (a trailing newline is trimmed). An external key always wins and is never copied into /data. The value is a path, never the key itself, so the key never appears in the Unraid XML or docker inspect. If secrets.bin exists but no key can open it (no key, a malformed key or the wrong key), the app refuses to start.
